constraint_review: No grid electricity; solar energy only: met — design yields 13.5 kWh per day from 3.6 kWp at 5.0 peak sun hours with 0.75 derate against reconciled electrical load 10.4 kWh per day with battery for night and cloudy day and no grid connection. Store about 1 tonne of fresh produce: met — design holds 1000 kg as 50 crates at 20 kg each in 8.64 m3 box with staged 250 kg per day intake discipline.
feedback:
Overall judgment: the working principle holds — sunlight to electricity to batteries to vapour-compression cold air over crates near 5 C is physically sound and has been demonstrated at 1.5 to 3 tonne in the cited Kenyan paper unit and ColdHubs product. My main worries are the hot-ambient COP claim resting on unopened datasheets, a small fan-heat accounting omission, and reliance on operational refusal to prevent full warm-tonne loading, but none breaks the concept on the numbers. I would release this to detail design with those points as design detailing, and the difference from prior art is as claimed a narrower 1-tonne staged 43 C split-array LFP plus R134a anchored PIR-box package, not a new principle.

Re-check of the four asks from the last loop. First, consistent daily energy in electrical units is now met: single thermal total 13.5 kWh per day (E109) with single curtain door 0.169 kWh per day (E110) converted by hot COP 1.40 to 10.4 kWh per day electrical (E111) confirmed term-by-term (E128) against 13.5 kWh per day yield from 3.6 kWp (E83). Second, night plus cloudy-day storage is now met: 10.0 kWh usable bank carries night load 3.02 kWh and ends at 3.73 kWh after one cloudy day at 4.05 kWh PV with surge check and low-voltage shed logic (E95), with nominal sizing at stated depth of discharge (E96) and 75 A charge current at 48 V (E97). Third, soil standing on a complete mass list is now met: complete mass 2210 kg (E118) split to chamber 1930 kg (E126) giving 23.2 kPa on six 400 mm pads (E127) below 150 kPa allowable (E62), with 1390 kg screw hold (E123) against 673 kg uplift (E90) on 17.6 sqm array (E84). Fourth, layout plus hot COP search is substantially met but weaker: dimensioned crate-airflow sketch exists (E124) with 50 vented 600 by 400 mm crates in 2.4 by 1.8 by 2.0 m box, while DC monoblock capacity and COP searches were performed but pages were never opened (E98-E103, E112-E113), so COP 1.40 remains plausible but unconfirmed by an opened datasheet.

Energy closure: I checked the physics relation by relation. Conduction uses Q equals U times A times dT with U about 0.21 W per sqm K for 100 mm PIR, area 25.4 sqm (E40) from 2 times length-times-width plus length-times-height plus width-times-height for 2.4 by 1.8 by 2.0 m interior 8.64 m3 (E39), dT 38 K for 43 C to 5 C, giving 203 W (E41) or 4.87 kWh per day thermal, which recomputes correctly and is ordinary — about two incandescent bulbs of leak. Staged pull-down uses Q equals m times c times dT with 250 kg times 3.6 kJ per kg K times 25 K equals 22,500 kJ equals 6.25 kWh thermal, which recomputes correctly. Respiration at 50 W per tonne gives 1.2 kWh per day, door with curtain sensible plus latent for 8 openings of 1.2 m3 each gives 0.102 plus 0.067 equals 0.169 kWh per day (E110), which recomputes correctly. Electrical uses refrigeration thermal divided by COP plus direct fan plus controls, giving 12.491 divided by 1.40 plus 0.96 plus 0.48 equals 10.36 kWh per day rounded to 10.4 kWh per day (E111), which recomputes correctly. Yield uses Ppk times peak sun hours times performance ratio with 3.6 times 5.0 times 0.75 equals 13.5 kWh per day (E83), which recomputes correctly, leaving about 3.1 kWh margin. The fault is that fan heat inside the box at 40 W for 24 h equals 0.96 kWh thermal is counted in the 13.5 kWh thermal sum (E109) but omitted from the numerator divided by COP in the electrical sum, understating electrical by 0.96 divided by 1.40 equals 0.69 kWh per day. Corrected electrical is about 11.1 kWh per day, still below 13.5 kWh per day yield, so the margin shrinks but the concept still closes. COP 1.40 at 38 K lift is about 19 percent of Carnot COP of 278 divided by 38 equals 7.3, which is plausible for a small R134a monoblock and does not violate thermodynamics, but because the supporting pages were never opened it should be confirmed by an opened datasheet in detail design.

Worst case: staged 250 kg per day at 43 C is shown, but full 1000 kg warm loading needs 25 kWh thermal pull-down and totals about 23.8 kWh per day electrical by the same relation, far above 13.5 kWh per day yield, so the design only holds if full loading is operationally prevented by the stated 8-opening single-crate discipline with 51st-crate and full-tonne refusal plus strip curtain and attendant log. That procedural control is acceptable at concept for a staffed cooperative but must remain a hard operating limit and placard. One cloudy day is shown to stay positive at 3.73 kWh remaining; two successive cloudy days would deplete the 10 kWh usable bank and must shed via low-voltage disconnect, which is stated but surge current in amps remains unquantified. Soil at 23.2 kPa is less than foot pressure of a person standing and far below 150 kPa allowable, so even if allowable were half the cited value on truly soft ground it still passes. Wind uplift at 25 m per s gust uses q equals 0.5 times rho times v squared equals 375 Pa with force q times 17.6 sqm equals 6600 N equals 673 kg mass equivalent (E90), held by eight 1.7 kN screws equals 1386 kg (E123) with factor about 2, which recomputes correctly.

Agreement and flows: parts, connections, loads and sequence agree — nine 400 W modules split 2 on roof gantry plus 7 on ground frame charging via MPPT to 48 V bank powering monoblock blowing rear-high to low-return over two rack rows with door and curtain, regulated by return-air plus produce probes. Check (0) every function has a means: convert with split array, store with LiFePO4 bank, remove heat with monoblock plus airflow plus eutectic buffer, enclose with PIR box, hold with racking plus 50 crates, regulate with thermostat plus probes, support with pads plus anchors. Check (1) size and mass limits by sum: produce 1000 kg plus crates 93.5 kg plus racking 90 kg plus panels 306 kg plus door plus battery plus eutectic plus monoblock plus frames plus wiring totals 2210 kg (E118), chamber subset 1930 kg (E126) on 0.96 sqm gives 23.2 kPa (E127); 50 crates at 0.24 sqm each stacked 5 high in two rows fit in 4.32 sqm floor and 8.64 m3 with 25 mm gaps and 900 mm door swing per sketch. Check (1b) numbered constraints are computed, not words only: 1000 kg from 50 times 20 kg (E49), 12.5 crates per day staged (E78), 13.5 versus 10.4 kWh per day, 23.2 versus 150 kPa, 1390 versus 673 kg. Check (2) two values: the board explored older thermals 12.8 and 13.2 and doors 0.44 and 0.66 and electricals 10.6 and 10.7, but the proposal commits to single controlling values 13.5 thermal with 0.169 door to 10.4 electrical, and dependent yield-margin and autonomy use those; anchor error 0.133 in one calc (E122) is superseded by correct 1390 kg (E123), and pressure 28.5 kPa putting all mass on six pads (E125) is conservative versus correct split paths. Check (3) flows trace end to end: sun to array to MPPT to battery to compressor plus fans to cold air to crates with sealed penetration plus trapped drain, and sensor to thermostat hysteresis to switched power plus shed to attendant log, with no missing step and no part in two places. Check (4) no blocking objection remains: the meeting closed by chief decision with all four members ready and no open objections, so the room is settled. Deviations noticed: fan-heat omission 0.69 kWh, unopened sources for soil and U-value and module size (E62, E32-E33, E64) and COP, and conservative foundation pressure — none changes the pass at concept given margins, but detail design should open the monoblock datasheet at 43 C, add fan heat to the COP numerator, quantify start surge and low-voltage shed setpoints, and field-verify screw pull and 250 kg pull-down uniformity as advised, not as acceptance conditions.
